I can never remember ImageMagick's flags. Something like this:
magick mogrify -path out -format webp -quality 80 -resize 1600x1600\> -unsharp 0x1 photos/*.jpg

I don't think I've ever typed that correctly from memory. So I made photu, where the same pipeline is just normal shell pipes:
photu read "photos/*.jpg" | photu resize 1600 | photu sharpen | photu write "out/{name}.webp" quality=80

You can chain as many of these as you want:
photu read "photos/*.jpg" \
| photu resize 1600 \
| photu crop 1200x630 gravity=center \
| photu rotate -3 background=white \
| photu adjust saturation=1.3 hue=15 \
| photu sharpen \
| photu overlay logo.png gravity=southeast opacity=0.35 \
| photu pad 24 color=white \
| photu write "social/{name}.webp" quality=82

The pipe between stages isn't actually carryin…
articles.title: I built a CLI so I'd stop typing ImageMagick flags wrong.

Dagster AuthKit is a community auth/RBAC wrapper for self-hosted Dagster OSS — no fork, no code changes, just wraps dagster-webserver. v0.4.0 just shipped a big security hardening pass plus cross-pod session revocation. This post is mostly a technical breakdown of what changed and a direct ask for help: there are specific issues and PRs where I need eyes from people who actually run this stuff in production.

articles.author: Felipe L
articles.description:
The shape of a real n8n agent


Most tutorials show an agent as one node: trigger goes in, magic AI node does everything, result comes out. Production systems don't look like that. They look like five distinct pieces:
Trigger — a webhook, form submission, schedule, or inbound email.
Retrieval (optional) — pull the context the model needs: a CRM record, a support ticket history, a row from Google Sheets.
Reasoning step — the LLM call that decides what to do, given the trigger and retrieved context.
Tool call(s) — the action the agent decided on: send a Slack message, update a CRM field, create a calendar event.
Human-in-the-loop checkpoint — a pause before anything that can't be undone (sending an email to a customer, charging a card, deleting a record).
Skip step 5 and you don't have an ag…
articles.title: How to Build Your First Production AI Agent with n8n

articles.author: Felipe L
articles.description:
What happened


Microsoft folded AutoGen — its research-driven multi-agent conversation framework — into Semantic Kernel, its enterprise agent SDK, and shipped the result as a single Microsoft Agent Framework in October 2025. AutoGen is now in maintenance mode: it still gets security patches, but new features and new projects are directed to Agent Framework instead.
This isn't a rename. AutoGen and Semantic Kernel had genuinely different design centers — AutoGen optimized for flexible, research-friendly multi-agent conversations; Semantic Kernel optimized for enterprise SDK consistency across Python, C#, and Java, with tighter Azure integration. Agent Framework is Microsoft's attempt to keep AutoGen's conversation patterns while giving them Semantic Kernel's production and governance story…
articles.title: AutoGen Is in Maintenance Mode — Migrating to Agent Framework

That premise is gone. So I moved the orchestrator out of Main Claude and into an agent.

articles.author: Sergey Boyarchuk
articles.description:
Introduction


Validating the structure of an HTML document goes beyond mere syntax checking. While tools like ANTLR excel at ensuring that tags are properly nested and attributes are correctly formatted, they fall short when it comes to enforcing specific element arrangements. For instance, ensuring that an <html> tag always contains exactly one <head> and one <body>, or that a <head> only includes valid <title>, <style>, or <script> elements, requires a more nuanced approach.
ANTLR’s core functionality lies in lexical and syntactic analysis, which involves tokenizing the input HTML and constructing a parse tree based on predefined grammar rules. However, structural validation demands context-sensitive checks that ANTLR’s context-free grammar cannot inherently provide. For example, while …
